title: Reduce with BinaryOperator and IntBinaryOperator

blocks.text: `BinaryOperator<T>` combines two values of one type into a third of that type, which is exactly what `Stream.reduce` needs. `BinaryOperator.maxBy(comparator)` builds one that keeps the larger of two values. `IntBinaryOperator` is the primitive form, `(int, int) -> int`, used by `IntStream.reduce` with no boxing.

items: `longest(List<String> words)` returns the longest word, reducing with `BinaryOperator.maxBy`.
`product(int[] values)` returns the product of the values, reducing with an `IntBinaryOperator`.

blocks.text: Think about what each method should return for an empty input, and which word wins when two are equally long (the earlier one).

cases.says: The longest word is found with a maxBy BinaryOperator.
The product of the values is folded with an IntBinaryOperator.
With no words there is no longest word: the Optional is empty.
Among equally long words, the first one wins.
The product of no values is 1, the identity of multiplication.

concepts: A BinaryOperator combines two values of one type, as reduce needs, and maxBy builds one that keeps the larger.
reduce without an identity returns an Optional, which is empty for an empty stream.
IntBinaryOperator and the other primitive forms work on ints directly, with no boxing.
